Stated Claim / Post Context:
WSMV4 investigative reporter featured on Today Show in recognition of National Murrow Award for ‘Murders on Main Street’ podcast

WSMV4 Investigative Reporter Jeremy Finley and General Manager Jasmine Hardin were among several people from NBC affiliates from across the country who appeared on the Today Show on Monday.

Actual Article Body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WSMV) - WSMV4 Investigative Reporter Jeremy Finley and General Manager Jasmine Hardin were among several people from NBC affiliates from across the country who appeared on the Today Show on Monday.

They attended the show while in New York to receive National Murrow Awards.

Finley is being recognized for the WSMV4 Investigates podcast “Murders on Main Street,” which is based on his investigative reporting.

“Murders on Main Street” details the events that led to the arrest of an American Airlines pilot for a double murder in Pembroke, Kentucky.

The Edward R. Murrow Awards are administered by the Radio Television Digital News Association (RTDNA) and are considered among the most respected journalism honors in the world.

The awards recognize work that upholds the values and standards established by broadcast journalism pioneer Edward R. Murrow. Murrow Award-winning stories prioritize the public interest, serve as a catalyst for public discussion, and adhere to the RTDNA Code of Ethics.

This honor marks WSMV’s second Murrow Award in the podcast category in the last three years.
